subject: Pricing & batching follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing & batching follow-up

Hi Stephanie / Camila -

Thanks again for the demo today - that was super helpful. A few follow-ups from our side so we can align on cost expectations and next steps: 

1) Rough workload numbers (requested for your unit-econ calculations):
   - Monthly active users (MAU): ~1,000,000
   - Average requests per MAU / month: ~2 (product chat + occasional summarization)
   - Avg tokens per request: prompt ~250 tokens, response ~150 tokens => ~400 tokens per request
   - Expected monthly tokens: 1M * 2 * 400 = ~800M tokens/month

2) Latency SLO: target 99th pctl end-to-end for chat ~1500ms (we'd like <1s if possible for most flows)

3) Budget / target unit economics: our finance lead is estimating a budget target of $250-350 per 1M tokens (inclusive of model + infra). We want to understand what continuous batching assumptions you use to model that target and where the big levers are.

4) Concurrency / pattern questions: we have a steady baseline (70% of traffic between 6am-10pm PT) with predictable diurnal shape plus product-triggered bursts (campaigns) that can increase volume x2-3 for short windows. Most traffic is short chat turns (400 tokens avg) but we have a subset of longer summarization jobs (~2-3k tokens) that are scheduled/batchable.

Can you confirm whether your continuous batching model would meaningfully lower unit cost with this mix, and what assumptions (batching window, latency tradeoffs, required concurrency) you use for pricing? Also can you send a short example of what a trial/pilot looks like (in terms of telemetry you need)?

Attaching a quick CSV with our rough hourly forecast and a budget ranges sheet.

Thanks,
Jordan
Director of Product, Acme Health

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up

Jordan - really appreciate the clear numbers and the CSV, that helps a lot. Quick post-call recap + our assumptions and proposed next steps: 

Recap / high-level answers
- Estimated monthly tokens: ~800M (matches your calc) - good baseline for unit-econ modeling.
- Target $/1M tokens: $250-350 is reasonable for planning; final depends on model choice (open vs finetuned), quantization, and how much continuous batching we can realize.

Batching & concurrency assumptions (continuous batching model)
- Continuous batching works best with steady arrival rates and many small requests. With a mostly steady diurnal load + scheduled long jobs, you should see meaningful gains.
- Typical assumptions we use for planning: effective batching window ~10-350ms at the runtime layer (this is adaptive), which groups concurrent calls arriving within that window into a single GPU batch.
- Unit-cost impact: for 400-token avg requests with steady traffic, we've seen 20-345% reductions in per-token GPU compute compared to a naive per-request baseline; savings improve with higher concurrency and when requests align with the batching window.
- For your traffic mix (70% steady, periodic 2-3x bursts, some long scheduled jobs): continuous batching will capture most baseline traffic savings; scheduled long summarization jobs are ideal candidates for separate batch/queue paths (we can route them to lower-cost backfills).

Concurrency considerations
- To sustain low latency during bursts, we recommend configuring reserved concurrency lanes:
  - Baseline lane sized to handle your 95th pctl steady load with aggressive batching.
  - Burst lane to absorb campaign spikes; this may trade cost for latency but preserves SLOs.
- Ballpark for your numbers: expect to reserve tens-to-low-hundreds of concurrent inference streams depending on the target P99 latency and model size. We'll run a small sizing exercise once we see your hourly forecast.

Unit economics model (example)
- Inputs we use: model FLOPS profile, GPU type, token length distribution, batching efficiency (gain %), request arrival distribution, quantization level.
- Output: $/1M tokens split into compute + infra + service margin. For planning, using conservative 25% batching efficiency yields a modeled cost in the ~$300/1M token range for an open LLM; optimistic (40%+) batching + 8-bit quantization can push that below $250/1M.

Next steps / ask from your side
1) Share the hourly forecast CSV (you already attached - perfect) and any sample request payloads (typical prompt + response length distributions).
2) Approve a short pilot: we propose a 2-week pilot with production-like traffic (traffic mirroring) to measure realized batching efficiency and P99 latency. We'll instrument per-request traces and token-level cost breakdowns.
3) If pilot looks good, we can put together a scoped SOW and price band tied to measured batching efficiency and reserved capacity.

I'll loop in Marissa (cc) for pricing oversight and to prep a pilot SOW. I can run a quick internal sizing tomorrow and follow up with a draft SOW and a proposed pilot start date.

Thanks - happy to hop on another call if you want to walk through the forecast together.

-Stephanie
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up

Thanks Stephanie - that all makes sense. A couple clarifications before the pilot:

- For the pilot, we can mirror a 1% sample of production traffic to your endpoint for 2 weeks. Will that be sufficient to measure effective batching?
- Our internal target for unit economics (post-pilot) is to land between $220-300 / 1M tokens. If we see >30% batching efficiency in the pilot we should be in range.
- We'll attach the CSV and a sample payload (see estimates attached). We also attached a budget_ranges.xlsx that shows where procurement is comfortable.

One ask: can you include a sample SOW that shows how price bands would adjust based on measured batching efficiency? That will make procurement conversations much faster.

Thanks,
Jordan

Attachments: estimated-traffic.csv, budget_ranges.xlsx

Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up - pilot SOW & next steps

Jordan / Asha - looping in Marissa to own pricing and SOW.

Short answers:
- 1% traffic mirror for 2 weeks is absolutely a good starting point to measure real batching efficiency and P99 behavior; we'll instrument token-level cost and end-to-end latency.
- We'll produce a draft SOW that includes price bands tied to observed batching efficiency (example bands: <20% savings, 20-35%, >35%) and a mutually-agreed measurement method.

Deliverables we'll provide before pilot kickoff:
- Draft SOW (SOW-draft.pdf) showing price bands and pilot acceptance criteria.
- Pilot instrumentation plan (what traces/metrics we collect + dashboard access).
- Internal sizing note (how we sized reserved lanes for baseline vs burst).

Proposed timeline:
- Today/Tomorrow: Redwood provides draft SOW and instrumentation plan.
- Within 3 business days: Acme confirms pilot mirror config (1% sample) and legal signs NDAs / pilot addendum.
- Week of Aug 17: pilot kickoff (2 weeks).

Marissa - can you review the attached draft SOW and confirm if we can offer the introductory pilot pricing band (we typically layer a small platform fee for pilot measurement)? Happy to sync offline if you want a quick call.

Jordan/Asha - thanks again - we'll get the draft SOW over shortly.

Best,
Stephanie
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
